### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**29** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3`.

⛔ **9** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `5ec6b175ef94fcefd74cf37ba1a3a22faf80ee99` — the merge of head `b61479cef2fd9c792411795db9f3a9e83a542565` into base `7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 5ec6b175ef94fcefd74cf37ba1a3a22faf80ee99 && git checkout 5ec6b175ef94fcefd74cf37ba1a3a22faf80ee99
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 b61479cef2fd9c792411795db9f3a9e83a542565 && git checkout -B drift-repro 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3 && git merge --no-ff b61479cef2fd9c792411795db9f3a9e83a542565

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 7be32d39fa62bd6e0f7c0a0054569b22bfb3dfd3` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `b61479cef2fd9c792411795db9f3a9e83a542565`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.webhook-method-get-retired.ts + packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/auto-enqueuer.ts, packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts

PR #34239 (Fixes #34098), spec schema face plus the declared narrowing. Inputs read: card #34098 body and all five comments (triage 6899464029, ruling 6902187601, claims 6902286425 / 6902292087, dev report 6905346098); the PR body, file list (30 files) and net diff against `main`; the check-runs on this head. Cited code was read at the head with `git show`: `shared/retired-key.ts`, `migrations/types.ts`, `migrations/entries/README.md`, `declared-webhooks.ts`, and service-messaging's `messaging-service.ts`, `sql-http-outbox.ts`, `http-sender.ts`, `http-outbox.ts`. Nothing was built or run.

Remainder, the lane seat's ACCEPT at TIER_DEFAULT and not judged in ④: the two test files, the 21 generated translation files, the two docs pages and the changeset body's prose. They were read only where a ① or ② judgment needed them.

Check-runs on the head: 68 runs, every conclusion `success` or `skipped`, none failed or pending. Passing runs include Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Test UI 1/16 to 16/16, Dogfood Regression Gate, Spec property liveness, Check Changeset, Governed Surface Queue Guard, PR-body guards, Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Type Check UI and Build Docs. The skipped runs are opt-in or conditional: 18.x upgrade harness, Packed-tarball smoke, Temporal Conformance, Lint UI, Dogfood Verify CLI, UI Published Artifacts, Queue verdict and Borrowed queue verdict, the schedule gate, and the unexpanded Dogfood Regression Gate matrix job. The request states one Test UI shard was re-run; the check-runs as they stand show it green.

### ① Derived judgments

- `WebhookSchema.method` accept-set goes from `GET` / `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` / `DELETE` to `POST` / `PUT` / `PATCH` / `DELETE`, default `POST` unchanged. Right, and declared (`Clause-②: no (narrowing)`, `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`). `enumWithRetiredValues` returns the prescription only for an own-property string hit, so `GET` gets the prescription and every other unknown value (`TRACE`, lower-case `get`, which the spec never admitted) keeps zod's own message.
- Every holder of `WebhookSchema` inherits the narrowing: `StackSchema.webhooks` (`defineStack`), `defineWebhook`, the `webhook` metadata type (`kernel/metadata-type-schemas.ts`, so the meta save door refuses GET too) and `DeclaredWebhookSource.parseItem`. Right: this is the intended break, and the PR body and changeset name the declared surface.
- The published type `Webhook['method']` loses `'GET'`, so a TypeScript consumer holding that literal stops compiling. Right, and covered by the BREAKING banner. No export is added or removed: `WEBHOOK_METHOD_GET_RETIRED` is module-private, which matches the unchanged `api-surface/`, `authorable-surface/` and `json-schema.manifest/` baselines (the authorable row `automation/Webhook:method` stands).
- The D3 registry gains one entry, `webhook-method-get-retired`, in `MIGRATIONS_BY_MAJOR[18].semantic`. Right: the file name follows the README rule (protocol major, then the id), the shape is the sibling shape (`id`, `surface`, `replacement`, `reason`, `acceptanceCriteria`), and no index is edited because the registry is generated from the directory. `relevantWhen` is correctly omitted, since the surface also lives in `sys_webhook` rows outside the stack, so the entry is always listed. `conversionIds` is correctly omitted, since there is no D2 conversion.
- The `sys_webhook` `method` select goes from five options to four. Right, and it is ruling A's second surface (Fable E3). Reads are unaffected: the SQL drivers build no enum or CHECK constraint from select options, and the new test reads a stored `get` back through both driver and engine.
- Translations: 21 deletions, 0 additions (11 `get: "GET"` leaves and 10 source hashes; `en` has no hash file). Right: deletions only, as stated.
- Dispatcher: a stored row whose method upper-cases to `GET` now produces one `dead` `sys_http_delivery` row per matched event and one `error` log per subscription. Right; see ④ for the path.
- No new error code. The park carries the standard-catalog pair `VALIDATION_ERROR`/400 (`spec/api/errors.zod.ts`), the same pair `webhook-legacy-cleartext.ts` carries on its delivery door. Right.
- The prescription names `@objectstack/spec 18.6.0`. Right: spec is `18.5.0` on main and on the head, eight pending changesets on main already grade spec `minor`, and this one does too, so the next release is 18.6.0.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/34098-webhook-method-get-retired.md` grades `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/plugin-webhooks` `minor`. That is correct under AGENTS.md Post-Task step 3: the level follows the `Metadata-protocol` kind alone, `narrowed` takes at least `minor` on a package the diff moves, and both packages are moved. `major` is not available: `check-changeset-no-major` refuses it in the launch window, and the fixed group would apply it to every package. The claim's phrase "a major-marked changeset" was the wrong instruction and the dev's deviation (2) is the right reading. The break is carried where step 3 puts it: the `!` title, the BREAKING banner, the FROM/TO lines with the one-line fix, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker (`registered webhook-method-get-retired`) whose id matches the new entry. Both declaration lines appear line-initial in the PR body and the changeset body and agree. The `Check Changeset` and `PR-body guards` check-runs concluded `success`.

Clause-②: no (narrowing). Correct: a value an author could write is now refused, and nothing is widened.

### ③ Boundary flags

- `open_questions` in dev report 6905346098 is empty. Nothing to escalate.
- Deviation 1, surface grew by the semantic entry and the spec pin: accepted. The ruling orders "an ADR-0087 marker with a D3 migration note"; with `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` the registered marker needs an entry file, and the README makes a new file the only way to add one. The pin is a test in the spec's existing file.
- Deviation 2, `minor` instead of `major`: accepted, see ②.
- Deviation 3, main not re-merged before open: accepted. `mergeable_state` is `clean`. Main is at `b8456ebd`; none of the 299 files it changed since the merge base is under `plugin-webhooks`, `service-messaging`, `automation/webhook*`, `shared/retired-key.ts` or the migration chain. Its three new semantic entries have different ids, and the directory layout exists so that such additions merge without conflict.
- Dev-noted items needing no ruling: the attribution HTML comment on body line 1 and the ADR-0087 marker comment (both mandated); the model-free commit trailer; the unlocked gate sweep; one heap re-run of `check:generated`; and the save-door test asserting the engine's `VALIDATION_FAILED` without measuring the REST 400. The 400 is the standard mapping of that code, so the docs and the entry may state it.
- Out-of-scope finding (the redeliver `DELIVERY_NEVER_SENT` text blames the signing secret for every park): filed as #34243, open. Answered; N1 below adds two sibling sentences to it.
- Sequencing: PR #34067 is on main and in this branch. A parked GET never reaches the #34067 refusal (④), so neither PR depends on the other for correctness. Shipping them in the same release is still right: with #34067 alone, a GET row leaves a lost-event log line and no delivery row.
- The PR is still a draft. That is a landing-state matter for the seat and no part of this verdict.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/automation/webhook.zod.ts` (schema face), against ruling 6902187601 and its first consumer.** Holds. The ruling orders GET out of the spec enum, leaves HEAD alone, and orders a D3 note because no lossless conversion exists. The code does exactly that with the repo's value-level retirement kit rather than a bare enum, so the refusal carries the prescription (step 3's tombstone requirement, applied to a value). The prescription follows the kit's convention: the value, the release, the reason, the one-line fix. Every sentence of the jsdoc checks against the tree: "every delivery sends the event envelope as the request body" is both enqueue sites in `auto-enqueuer.ts`; "a stored GET subscription is parked by the dispatcher with the reason on a dead delivery row; its method is never rewritten" is `parseRow` plus `recordUndeliverable`, and nothing in the diff writes `sys_webhook.method`. The first consumer, `DeclaredWebhookSource.parseItem`, wraps `WebhookSchema.parse` in a catch that warns once per name with the zod message (which now includes the prescription) and skips the item, so a GET declaration cannot crash a refresh. Attempt to break it: `.default('POST')` still applies on the wrapped enum, and the pin reads `WebhookSchema.shape.method.unwrap().options` and the default (Test Core green). The guard `typeof issue.input === 'string'` plus `hasOwnProperty` means a non-string or prototype-named input cannot pick up the retirement text.

**`packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.webhook-method-get-retired.ts`, against its siblings and the registry.** Holds. Shape, file name and scaffolding match the README, and the comment block sits directly above `export const entry` so it reaches the generated table. Read sentence by sentence against the tree: both surfaces are named; "refused 400 `VALIDATION_FAILED` by the select" is the engine validator's code with its standard status; "keeps loading and is parked ... dead row with 0 attempts ... nothing is sent" is the measured path; "never converted, at load, at save or by a migration" is true, since there is no conversion entry and no write. The acceptance criteria are checkable by the owner (`os validate`, the data list, the delivery row).

**The narrowing, against the published spec on main and ruling A.** It makes the spec's own refusal real and takes no working capability away. On main the spec advertises GET while every delivery carries a body, so no GET webhook ever delivered (card evidence; `http-sender.ts`). ADR-0049 and ADR-0078 point the same way, and the maintainer chose A. The build is ruling A as written, with Fable E2 (HEAD untouched), E3 (both surfaces, every locale's `options.get`, the docs row) and E4 (park through `parkedReason`, never convert) applied.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/auto-enqueuer.ts`, every producer path.**

- Stored rows: `parseRow` computes `String(row.method ?? defn.method ?? 'POST').toUpperCase()` and parks when the result is `GET`. `get`, `GET` and `Get` all park, and so does a row whose method lives only in `definition_json`. The method is carried through unchanged.
- Refresh loop: a parked row is reported, cached and skipped before `attachCredentials`, so it holds no secret and no header map (the #8069 park rule) and no later credential park can overwrite its reason. A healthy row clears the say-once entry, so a row that is fixed and broken again is reported again.
- Declared webhooks: `projectDeclared` goes through the same `parseRow` and returns before `splitWebhookSecret` / `splitWebhookHeaders`, so a declaration handed in past the schema is parked with no credentials.
- Both enqueue sites, per-record and bulk, pass `undeliverableReason: sub.parkedReason` (unchanged lines). The organization filter runs before them, so a dead row never records another organization's event.
- The seam: `MessagingService.enqueueHttp` routes any input carrying a reason to `recordUndeliverable`, which goes straight to `insert` with `status: 'dead'`, `attempts: 0` and no signature. The #34067 refusal `assertBodylessPayloadAdmitted` lives only in `enqueue()` (memory and SQL outboxes), so a parked GET never meets it. The product wiring (`webhook-outbox-plugin.ts`) binds the messaging service, not the raw outbox.
- After the write: the dispatcher claims only `pending` rows, so nothing is fetched; `assertHttpRedeliverable` refuses a terminal row with 0 attempts; dedup on `(source, dedup_key)` gives one row per event per subscription.
- Log level: `error`, said once per subscription and pruned with the other two ledgers. This matches the #8069 precedent and the AGENTS.md question (the row keeps reading `active: true` while nothing is delivered), and the message carries the consequence and the fix.

Attempts to break it, all negative: a GET row with no triggers is refused earlier by the existing no-triggers path and matches no event; the record validator's option check runs over the values a write supplies (`record-validator.ts`), so a partial update that leaves `method` out, such as deactivating the row, is not blocked by the narrowed select; removing a select option creates no schema-sync hazard for stored `get` rows; the `GET` method recorded on the dead row is plain data on a system-context insert.

**`packages/plugins/plugin-webhooks/src/sys-webhook.object.ts`.** Holds. Four options, `defaultValue: 'post'` unchanged, and the comment's claims (the select is what refuses at save; a stored `get` is parked by `retiredMethodParkReason`; never rewritten) agree with the code.

One boundary of the park, stated so nobody over-reads it. The park reaches `sys_webhook` rows, which is what the ruling orders ("Stored GET rows"). A GET webhook held as a registry item (declared in code, or saved earlier through the meta save door) is refused at parse and skipped with one `warn` carrying the prescription; it gets no dead row. Fable §4 predicted exactly this consequence before the maintainer ruled, the changeset says it, and `warn` is the AGENTS.md level for a trigger that is not armed. Because the only in-repo reader parses through `WebhookSchema`, the `projectDeclared` park branch is defensive: it is reachable only by a reader that skips the schema, which is how the test reaches it.

No must-fix, no should-fix.

N1 (nit) — Three sentences in `auto-enqueuer.ts`, outside this diff's hunks, now describe only one kind of park: the `CachedSubscription.parkedReason` jsdoc ("Set when a credential ... could not be recovered"), and `reportWriteFailure`'s parked branch, whose `error` text says the subscription "is parked for an unresolvable credential". For a method-parked row whose dead-row write fails, that clause is false. This is the same class as #34243. Leave it on this head and add the two sentences to #34243; fixing them here would move the head.

N2 (nit) — The `retiredMethodReported` comment says "again after its method is fixed and it breaks again". That holds for rows (the refresh loop deletes the id on a healthy parse). The declared path never deletes it, so it does not hold there. No product path reaches that case, because a declared GET cannot pass the schema. Accepted deviation.

N3 (nit) — `content/docs/automation/webhooks.mdx`, "Stored GET webhooks are parked", covers the row and a declared webhook failing parse, but does not say that a webhook already held as a registry item (for example one saved through the meta save door before the upgrade) is skipped with a warning and gets no dead row. The changeset does say it. One sentence on the docs page would close it; this is a prose face and optional.
